questions.qtext:
A bank maintains checking account data in a relational database, while customer (owner) information is stored in a separate file system on a different server. An operation in performed that adds a new owner to the file system and associates that owner with a newly created account
in that database.
Assume there is no distributed transaction management between the database and the file system.
Which of the following is true regarding the ACID properties of this operation?

options.text: Atomicity is not guaranteed, as failure in one system may not roll back change in the other.
Isolation is not always ensured as the operations occurs independently on separate system.
Durability is satisfied only if both system independently ensure persistence after commit.
Consistency is always maintained, as each system handles its own constraints.

questions.solution:
(a, b, c)
DB + File system on another server:
Two independent systems:
• Relational data base
• Separate file system
No distributed transaction:
• Manager to co-ordinate them.
RDBMS server File System server
Required distributed
Transaction manager to coordinate system of RDBMS server, FS servers.

questions.qtext:
Consider a database with two data items X and Y and two concurrent transactions T1 and T2 operating as follows:

 


Which of the following statements is/are not true?

options.text: The schedule involves a read-write conflict, where T2 observes an unrepeatable read on X, violating isolation.
Transaction T1 performs a dirty read on X, violating isolation.
The schedule contain write-write conflict on X, T1 may over-write uncommitted data of T2 which causes lost update problem if T1 abort before T2 commit.
Under strict-2PL, schedule S would be allowed and prevent dirty read.

questions.solution:
(a, c, d)
• No unrepeatable read as T1 reads both X and Y before T1 perform any writes.
• If T2 abort at any stage, we can abort T1 as well to prevent atomicity and restart schedules.
• Strict-2PL, does not allow to run given schedule as their is a dirty read.

questions.qtext:
Let R(A) be a relation that contain both integer and NULL values in attribute A.
Consider the following two queries:
Query 1: SELECT FROM R WHERE A NOT IN (5, 10, NULL;)
Query 2: SELECT FROM R WHERE A <> 5 AND A <> 10 AND A IS NOT NULL;
Which of the following statements is/are false?

options.text: Query 1 and Query 2 return same tuples.
Query 1 will not return any tuple for any value of A.
Query 1 returns rows where A is not NULL and is neither 5 nor 10.
Query 2 will return all rows where A is neither 5 nor 10.

questions.solution:
(a, c, d)
• Query 1 always gives empty relation.
• Query 2 return tuples where A is not NULL, neither 5 nor 10.

Consider the following log file, contains log records of the following form.

 
Identify the correct statement.

options.text: Transaction T1, T3 redo and T2 undo after abort.
Transaction T2, T3 redo and T4 undo after abort.
Transaction T1 store permanently, T3 redo and T2, T4 undo.

questions.solution:

• T3 commit before abort so redo it.
• T2, T4 not commit till abort so undo them.
